title: The Massive Beam
text: “Why on earth are there so many traps? Imiya-dono, does anything about this ring a bell?”
“Um, well, I don’t know anything about these.”
“So they were set up afterward?”
“Iwatani-dono, do you have some idea?”
“No, but looking further ahead, it’s unnaturally suspicious—there are trees with spikes jutting out of the ground and things like that… More importantly, Motoyasu-kun!”
“Motoyasu-sama! Are you all right!?”
While Yuki-chan got up and tried to rush toward me, I stood up and brushed off the dust cloud, I say.
“What in the world is this?” I said.
I’d never seen anything like this before, indeed. Setting aside the spike trap from earlier, countless splintered pieces of wood with sharpened points were now stuck in the path ahead.
“Guess that’s what you get in a world with levels. Plus, feels like it’s the handiwork of someone with looping abilities?”
“More to the point, how is he acting completely unfazed after taking a hit like that, and not a scratch on him after falling?”
Crocodile Guy was muttering something, but there was no way a trap of that caliber could actually injure me, I say.
“For the Shield Hero, maybe, but… thinking too hard about it is probably pointless.”
“Motoyasu-sama! Thank goodness you’re unharmed!”
“Whoa… Imiya, be careful not to fall off Kou, okay?”
“Y-yeah. B-but you don’t need to squeeze my hands and feet with your wings so tight…”
Kou seemed to be gripping Mole’s hands and feet with his wings so she wouldn’t fall.
“It doesn’t seem like these are traps left behind by Imiya-chan and the other members of the Rūmo tribe… judging by Imiya-chan’s reaction.”
“So it would seem.”
Father had Filo-tan swiftly kick a pebble at a spot he was aiming for, revealing yet another pitfall trap this time. And how thoughtful of them—the bottom of the pit was lined with plenty of spikes.

“Judging by the trap types, they look like booby traps, bungee stakes, that sort of thing… but since it sounds like a fair number of heroes and people from other worlds have passed through here, it’s hard to say for certain. Just who set up traps like this… and it looks like they even rigged tripwire alarms.”
“How very thoughtful of them,” I said.
I climbed back onto Yuki-chan and listened to Father’s analysis.
“Might be quickest if I take the lead and just neutralize the traps with sheer durability…”
“That is not really a good idea.”

Crocodile Guy looked displeased at Father’s suggestion. Indeed, no matter how sturdy Father might be against this sort of thing, it wasn’t exactly the best approach. Come to think of it, in the original world, there was testimony that Father had once suggested simply smashing through a wall while clearing a facility belonging to the Three Heroes Church. Perhaps Father simply found the process of disarming traps too troublesome.
“Hmm. The one who’s good at this sort of thing is Lars-chan, but…”

Indeed, Panda was skilled at trap disarmament. More than that, there was no doubt Panda would absolutely be the type to set traps like this herself. If she ever made a pitfall as part of some coordinated maneuver, she’d without question plant bamboo inside to turn it into a proper bamboo trap.
“Ooh, an obstacle course? Sounds fuuun!”

Filo-tan said cheerfully. It did look like a fun obstacle course, honestly. Dangerous, sure, but for us with our enhanced abilities, clearing it would be no trouble at all. Big Sister’s friend seemed like the type who’d enjoy something like this too.
“Ehh, but if we play around and Imiya gets hurt, Kou no like.”
“Ehh…”

Oh ho, so Kou liked playing around, but hated the idea of Mole getting hurt. What wholesome growth. This Motoyasu is truly delighted to see Kou growing up so well. And it’s all thanks to Elephant, I say.
“Yuki-chan, is your leg all right?”
Yuki-chan was a racing-type Filolial-sama, so her legs were a bit more delicate compared to other Filolial-samas. Falls like that required some caution.
“I’m fine! More importantly, are you unharmed, Motoyasu-sama?”
“Not a problem in the world, I say.”
Yuki-chan, having become a Queen-class Filolial-sama, was quite sturdy, so I hadn’t been too worried, but it was good to see she wasn’t hurt. Just to be safe, I cast a light healing spell on her.
“There’s no doubt someone set these up, but…”
Father seemed to be pondering what to do.
“No need to worry, Father. Just stand back and watch calmly.”
“This flow of events… oi! The Spear Hero’s about to do something!”

Crocodile Guy seemed to be warning Father about something, but there was truly no need to worry, I say. If a trap like this dared to block our path, there was only one thing to do. I already had the distance to Mole’s tribe’s den memorized… and the fastest way to carve a path all at once was clear.
“Eh? Wait, Motoyasu-kun, what are you—”
“Here we go, I say! Liberation Fire Eye VII, I say!”
I chanted the spell, channeling power into my eyes.
“Motoyasuuu Massiiiive Beeeeaaaam, I saaaaay!”
I was, as ever, growing, evolving, transcending. This was no ordinary beam like before.
Somehow, the beam had gotten thicker!

In a flash, I bored through the trees and ground all the way near Mole’s den with the heat ray from my eyes! With a blast like that, the traps were rendered utterly meaningless. Ha ha ha! Indeed! Of course, I’d put out any wildfires afterward. KABOOM! I blasted right through. With a hisssss…, a path opened up all the way to the front of the den we were heading for.
“F-from his eyes…”
“Wow, that’s amazing!”
Filo-tan praised me! Ahem, indeed!
“I’ve given up objecting to amazing feats at this point, but this is her hometown, you know…”
Crocodile Guy seemed to be furrowing his brow, but I paid it no mind.
“Umm… so there’s a spell that shoots a mysterious beam from your eyes…”
“It’s my original spell, I say!”
“I—I see…”
“You did it!”
“Ooh, now we can go safely!”
Kou turned back toward Mole and smiled. Mole just stood there with a blank, dumbfounded expression.
“I suppose one can’t afford to be shocked every time by Kitamura-dono’s deeds anymore… but you’ve gone and blasted straight through the destination itself—is that really all right?”
“I would never make such a blunder, I say.”

Look who’s talking! In my mind, I could almost hear Ren, Itsuki, and Father—who once failed to save someone from a false accusation—pointing that out, but I would never make such a mistake, I say. Well, if Itsuki and Ren happened to be positioned right at the core when we cleared the Spirit Tortoise, I might blast right through them too! HAHAHA!
“W-well… it’s probably fine, so let’s go.”
And so, we arrived in front of Mole’s tribe’s den. As we approached, suddenly an arrow came flying at our feet. Yuki-chan sensed it instantly and leapt backward to dodge.
“Who goes there!” Yuki-chan called out.

The sniper showed no sign of answering. Where were they? Another arrow flew from a different location and struck me right in the head. Not a bit of pain, of course! My hair caught it clean. Chak! I say.
“Uh, um…”
“Don’t worry about it. According to Theo, we should just think of that one as an existence from an entirely different story—a gag manga, apparently.”

Crocodile Guy cut off Father, who seemed about to say something, but what on earth were they talking about? I’d thought the first arrow came from the den, but that wasn’t it. There was some presence lurking among the surrounding trees. Father and the others sensed it too and heightened their guard. But… hmm, hard to pin down. Troublesome. Should I just burn the whole area down with magic or a skill?
“What business do you humans have coming to a place like this…!”
A muffled voice echoed from somewhere among the trees.

“To burn down the forest… that’s the very definition of barbaric. Just as I thought, the Melromarc lot are… There are no slaves here for you to capture! I won’t tell you to leave. But now that you know of this place—!?”
The voice’s owner sounded, of all things, startled. What would happen now that we knew of this place? Now that we knew, there was only one thing to do—die.
“On closer inspection… it doesn’t seem you’re enemies after all. If you’re coming this way, all the better—I’ve been hoping to make contact. And your companion here is…”

The voice seemed to be reaching its own conclusions without consulting anyone. There was a rustling sound, and something leapt out from between the trees, landing with a light thud. A figure emerged, wrapped deeply in a robe, wearing goggles and a mask so thick it was impossible to tell who they were, armed to the teeth, carrying a bow nearly the same size as the one I’d had when I became an usaunny. The muffled voice was thanks to the mask. Judging by silhouette alone, this wasn’t a human—more like a small demi-human.
“Y-you are…?”
Father called out to the mysterious ambusher.
“Don’t move. If you act carelessly, I won’t show mercy even for Naofumi-san and the others.”
“You know who I am…?”
“Yes, I know a fair bit about you. I always figured we’d cross paths somewhere eventually…”
The hidden figure tugged off the robe’s hood, removed the goggles and mask, and slowly stepped closer, looking at Father and me.
“Ri—”
Oops, I nearly blurted it out without thinking. Standing there was none other than Itsuki, now turned riska.
